prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1210; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision reported by the insured. Claimant reports neck and back strain and states she was transported from the scene by ambulance. Claimant is represented by counsel; all contact to be routed through the attorney's office going forward. Initial liability appears clear based on the insured's statement and the police report, with the insured's vehicle striking the rear of the claimant's vehicle at low to moderate speed.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to acknowledge representation and request medical authorizations, prior treatment records for the neck and back, and wage information. Attorney indicated the claimant is currently attending physical therapy and expects a treatment plan update from her treating physician. Requested copies of all bills to date.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of both vehicles submitted by the insured. Rear bumper damage to the claimant's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact. Repair estimate received and under review. Vehicle is being assessed for a possible total loss threshold. Insured has been advised that liability is likely to be accepted on the property damage side pending final review.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the treating clinic and the initial imaging report. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm, no fracture noted. Treatment notes reflect ongoing complaints of stiffness and reduced range of motion. Forwarded records to the medical review unit for evaluation of reasonableness and relatedness. Follow-up with the attorney's office scheduled to discuss the settlement posture once treatment is complete.

Entry 5: Attorney's office submitted a demand package including medical bills, a summary of treatment, and a request for compensation for pain and suffering and lost wages. Demand is under review by claims supervisor. Noted that the claimant has not yet reached maximum medical improvement, so reserves will be maintained and no offer will be made until the treating physician issues a discharge or permanency opinion.
